abstract: Cellular sources of reproducible transcriptomic changes in diabetic foot ulcer (DFU) remain incompletely defined. This study integrated differential-expression analysis, weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) gene screening, exploratory machine-learning feature selection, two external bulk-transcriptomic datasets, single-cell analysis, traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) network analysis, and patient-tissue quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) and western blotting. In GSE199939 (10 DFU and 11 control samples), 3,691 differentially expressed genes were identified, and the WGCNA blue module was strongly associated with DFU (r = 0.97, p = 5 × 10-13). Intersecting the differentially expressed genes, blue-module hub genes, and 1,062 DPN-related genes yielded 77 candidates. CCL7, CHEK1, MKI67, MMP1, MMP13, and TRPV2 were supported by at least two feature-selection methods; complete separation in support vector machine recursive feature elimination raised concerns about discovery-cohort overfitting. MMP1 showed the largest discovery-cohort expression change (log2 fold change = 9.854; adjusted p = 1.24 × 10-29). In the merged GSE68183/GSE80178 matrix, MMP1 had an adjusted p of 0.0159 and an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.981. In GSE134431, MMP1 expression was nominally higher in DFU than in non-ulcerated diabetic foot skin (p = 0.0225; adjusted p = 0.135; AUC = 0.808). Analysis of 69,944 cells from 24 samples showed the highest mean MMP1 expression in fibroblasts, with higher sample-level expression in DFU fibroblasts, keratinocytes, and endothelial cells. Patient-tissue assays showed higher MMP1 mRNA abundance in four matched pairs (paired test on ΔCq, p = 3.04 × 10-5) and higher protein abundance in three matched pairs (paired p = 0.0107). Statistical replication was incomplete. Findings suggest a fibroblast-centered matrix-remodeling association, subject to limitations from transcripts per million (TPM) input in count-based discovery analysis, incomplete single-cell preprocessing records, and small tissue-assay cohorts. Causality and clinical utility remain unestablished.
